title: Local Isotonic Drinks Every Southeast Asian Runner Should Know
seo_title: Local Isotonic Drinks for Southeast Asia Runners
meta_description: 100Plus, Isoplus, Sponsor, Pocari Sweat -- the regional isotonic drinks that outsell imported sports drinks across Southeast Asia, and why runners reach for them.
dek: Long before imported sports drinks arrived, Southeast Asia had its own isotonic staples -- sold at every convenience store, sponsoring national teams, and often cheaper and more available than anything shipped in. Here's what's actually in reach on race day.

sections.heading: Why Regional Isotonic Drinks Matter More Here Than Elsewhere
paragraphs: In most Western running markets, isotonic and electrolyte drinks are a specialty-store purchase. Across Southeast Asia, the opposite is true: brands like 100Plus, Isoplus, and Sponsor are convenience-store staples that have been part of daily life for decades, which means they're almost always the easiest hydration option available on the actual day of a race -- at the finish-line table, the corner shop near your hotel, or the aid station itself.

That availability matters more than brand loyalty. A runner who trains with an imported electrolyte brand but can only find a regional one at a race in a smaller city is better off knowing what these local drinks actually contain and how they compare, rather than discovering the difference mid-race.

sections.heading: Malaysia and Singapore's 100Plus
paragraphs: 100Plus has been Malaysia and Singapore's dominant isotonic drink since 1983, when F&N launched it to mark the company's 100th year in Asia -- it's been voted the top isotonic brand in both markets repeatedly since. It's officially endorsed by Malaysia's National Sports Council and has sponsored elite athletes across multiple sports, which is part of why it's the drink handed out at so many regional races.

The original carbonated formula and the newer 100PLUS Active (non-carbonated) cover slightly different preferences -- carbonation isn't ideal mid-run for most people, so Active is the better pick to actually drink while moving, with the original better saved for post-race.

sections.heading: Indonesia's Isoplus and Strive-Adjacent Nutrition
paragraphs: Isoplus, made by Indonesia's Wings Food, is one of the country's dominant isotonic brands alongside Pocari Sweat, built around a 7-ion formula and sold in small, race-friendly 350ml bottles. Wings has leaned further into running specifically with the Isoplus Run event series, which is as clear a signal as any that the brand sees runners as a core audience rather than an afterthought.

Indonesia is also home to Strive, generally credited as the country's first locally-produced energy gel -- worth knowing about even in a hydration-focused list, since pairing a local isotonic drink with a local gel is a genuinely all-Indonesian fueling strategy for anyone racing there.

sections.heading: Thailand's Sponsor and the Region's Pocari Sweat
paragraphs: Sponsor has been Thailand's leading sports drink for more than 30 years, made by TCP Group (also behind the original Thai formula that became Red Bull) and used as the official drink of the Thai national football team. Its newer Sponsor Isotonic line specifically targets the lower-sugar, quick-refresh profile that suits endurance activity better than the classic formula.

Pocari Sweat deserves a mention across the whole region rather than one country -- while the brand originates with Japan's Otsuka Pharmaceutical, it's manufactured and marketed so heavily across Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and beyond that it functions as a de facto regional staple, sold in both ready-to-drink bottles and travel-friendly powder sachets.

faqs.question: Are local isotonic drinks like 100Plus or Isoplus as effective as imported sports drinks?
faqs.answer: Yes -- they're built around the same core principle of replacing fluid and electrolytes lost through sweat, using broadly similar sodium and potassium profiles. The main practical difference is availability: these regional brands are sold at nearly every convenience store and race aid station across the region, which often matters more than marginal formula differences.

faqs.question: Should I drink a carbonated isotonic drink like original 100Plus during a run?
faqs.answer: Generally no -- carbonation can cause bloating or discomfort mid-run for most people. Non-carbonated versions like 100PLUS Active are the better choice to drink while moving; the classic carbonated formula is better saved for after you've finished.

faqs.question: Is Pocari Sweat a Southeast Asian brand?
faqs.answer: Not originally -- it's made by Japan's Otsuka Pharmaceutical -- but it's manufactured and sold so extensively across Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and neighboring countries that it functions as a regional staple alongside genuinely homegrown brands like 100Plus, Isoplus, and Sponsor.
